source_text: Sed et Saturus benedictus hanc uisionem suam edidit, quam ipse conscripsit. Passi, inquit, eramus, et exiuimus de carne, et coepimus ferri a quattuor angelis in orientem, quorum manus nos non tangebant. Ibamus autem non supini sursum uersi, sed quasi mollem cliuum ascendentes. Et liberato primo mundo uidimus lucem immensam, et dixi Perpetuae (erat enim haec in latere meo): Hoc est quod nobis dominus promittebat: percepimus promissionem. Et dum gestamur ab ipsis quattuor angelis, factum est nobis spatium grande, quod tale fuit quasi uiridiarium, arbores habens rosae et omne genus flores. Altitudo arborum erat in modum cypressi, quarum folia cadebant sine cessatione. Ibi autem in uiridiario alii quattuor angeli fuerunt, clariores ceteris: qui ubi uiderunt nos honorem nobis dederunt, et dixerunt ceteris angelis: Ecce sunt, ecce sunt, cum admiratione. Et expauescentes quattuor illi angeli, qui gestabant nos, deposuerunt nos. Et pedibus nostris transiuimus stadium uia lata. Ibi inuenimus Iocundum et Saturninum et Artaxium, qui eadem persecutione uiui arserunt, et Quintum, qui et ipse martyr in carcere exierat; et quaerebamus de illis ubi essent ceteri. Dixerunt nobis angeli: Uenite primum intro et salutate dominum.
thought_title: Carried East to a Garden of Light
orientation: Saturus, the fellow Christian who surrendered himself for the group, now speaks in his own first-person report after Perpetua's diary stops the day before the public games.
pass_a_gloss: But also blessed Saturus published this vision of his, which he himself wrote out. "We had suffered," he said, "and we went out from the flesh, and we began to be carried by four angels toward the east, whose hands were not touching us. And we were going not turned over upward on our backs, but as if climbing a gentle slope. And when the first world was left behind we saw an immense light, and I said to Perpetua (for she was at my side): 'This is what the lord was promising to us: we have received the promise.' And while we were being carried by those same four angels, there came to be for us a great open space, which was such as a garden, having rose trees and every kind of flowers. The height of the trees was in the manner of a cypress, whose leaves were falling without ceasing. But there in the garden four other angels were, brighter than the rest: who when they saw us gave honor to us, and said to the other angels: 'Here they are, here they are,' with wonder. And having become afraid those four angels who were carrying us put us down. And with our feet we crossed a stadium by a broad road. There we found Jucundus and Saturninus and Artaxius, who in the same persecution burned alive, and Quintus, who also himself as a martyr had departed in prison; and we were asking about them where the rest were. The angels said to us: 'Come first inside and greet the lord.'"

pass_b_english: Blessed Saturus also published this vision of his, which he wrote out himself. "We had suffered death," Saturus says, "and we had left the flesh, and four angels began to carry us eastward, yet their hands never touched us. We traveled not on our backs with our faces turned upward, but as if we were climbing a gentle slope. Once we had left the first world behind, we saw an immense light, and since Perpetua was at my side I said to her, 'This is what the Lord was promising us. We have received the promise.'"

While those same four angels were still carrying us, a great open space appeared before us, like a garden planted with rose trees and flowers of every kind. The trees stood as tall as cypresses, and their leaves kept falling without ceasing. Four other angels waited there in the garden, brighter than the rest.

When they saw us, they gave honor to us and said in wonder to the other angels, "Here they are! Here they are!" At this the four angels carrying us grew awestruck and set us down. Then we crossed a full stadium on foot by a broad road. There we found Jocundus and Saturninus and Artaxius, who had been burned alive in that same persecution, and Quintus, who had also died in prison as a martyr, and we asked them where the others were. The angels told us, "Come inside first and greet the Lord."
